_about: Exposure-weighted risk and repair equity. These are illustrative starting values chosen by judgement, not validated safety measurements. Copy this file and point ROADSENSE_EXPOSURE_RULES_FILE at the copy to change them; every risk score records the hash of the rules it used.

weights._about: Share of the overall score. Exposure is a PROXY from nearby infrastructure, not measured traffic: a school or bus stop nearby is not proof of pedestrians or passengers.

distances_m._about: A feature counts only within this distance of the defect. Its relevance falls linearly from 1 at the defect to 0 at the limit.

relevance._about: Multiplier for how directly a feature relates to the damaged road. A bike lane tagged on the same road is direct; a separate path nearby may not share the carriageway; a school is only a reason to expect people on foot.

physical._about: Physical severity 0..1 from the existing severity model: the severity band (S1-S4, from the estimated width for potholes and the box area for cracks) times a class factor, plus a small boost for repeat sightings by independent drivers. Depth is never measured from video. Detector confidence is shown alongside but never changed.

road_context._about: OSM road class as a stand-in for traffic speed and volume (no traffic counts exist).

categories._about: overall >= high is High, >= medium is Medium, else Low. Critical needs both overall >= critical AND the severity model's most urgent band, so exposure alone can never make a minor defect Critical.

equity._about: A neighbourhood is flagged for a POSSIBLE difference in service delivery only when its median repair time is at least min_ratio times the rest of the city's, a Mann-Whitney U test gives p < alpha, and both groups have at least min_sample completed repairs. A flag is a question to look into, not a finding of unfair treatment.
